- File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 251-258 (initialization) and line 324 (cache population check)
  Problem: The `POST_MERGE_DISPATCH` variable is initialized to `"false"` at line 252 but is never set to `"true"` based on the fetched `pr_merged` value. The cache population logic at line 324 checks `if [ "${POST_MERGE_DISPATCH}" = "true" ]`, but since `POST_MERGE_DISPATCH` is never updated from its initial `"false"` value, the caching logic is dead code.
  Why it fails at runtime: When a PR is merged, the gate job should populate `POST_MERGE_PR_TEXT_JSON` and `POST_MERGE_LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` with already-fetched metadata, but it doesn't because the `POST_MERGE_DISPATCH` check never passes. This forces the post-merge validate dispatch job to always fall back to live API calls instead of using cached values, failing the MERGE-001 acceptance criteria.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 285-302 (expanded --jq to object + per-field jq -r extractions)
  Problem: The PR metadata fetch now requests a JSON blob and then invokes `jq -r` six separate times (state, merged, head_ref, labels, additions, deletions, title, body) instead of one `--jq '@tsv'` with a single `IFS read`.
  Why it fails at runtime: No functional failure, but each extra `jq -r` subshell adds fork/exec overhead on every gate evaluation. Given this runs on every review_autofix trigger, the cumulative cost is measurable compared to the original single-tsv parse.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "late ready-to-merge / review-blocked steps still fall back to extra `/pulls/{PR_NUMBER}` reads even though `PR_META_FILE` was already collected"
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml — late ai:ready-to-merge and ai:review-blocked label step blocks (around lines 2130-2145 in the workflow)

  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
